A1.justification: Both PDFs contain the same study, with all 22 pages and Appendices A–L available. Pages 2–22 have identical extracted text and rendered images; page 1 differs only in the resource footnote and arXiv version/date stamp.

before.justification: v3 reports original model experiments on four creative-generation tasks, human evaluations, and supplementary analyses, including Tables 3–5 and appendix Tables B.2, H.1 and K.1.

after.justification: v4 retains those original model experiments, human evaluations, pilot analyses and LLM-as-a-Judge results in the main text and appendices.

M1.justification: Sections 4–5 retain identical sequential generation, length-controlled preference filtering, Diverse-NS-Lite proxies and DPO training. No algorithm steps or model components change.

E1.justification: The synthetic story-writing training data and Divergent Associations, Persona Generation, Alternate Uses and Creative Writing tasks are unchanged, including the human and LLM-judge evaluation scenarios.

E2.justification: Base-model and DivPO comparators, and comparisons between D-NS and D-NS-Lite, remain identical within corresponding experiments, including Tables 3–5 and K.1. Appendix E's DivPO implementation is unchanged.

E3.justification: The 3,000-pair training budget, model configurations, sampling procedures, sample counts, metrics and judging protocols are identical in Sections 5–6 and the appendices.

E4.justification: The metric-correlation and filtering analyses, sequential-prompting pilot, response-length analysis and qualitative story examples are unchanged in Tables 1–2, Appendices B and G, and Figure L.1.

E5.justification: Seed descriptions, standard-deviation reporting and independent t-tests remain identical, including Table 4 and Tables G.1 and H.1. No run information or uncertainty procedure is added or revised.

E6.justification: All numerical entries, plotted results and example responses match across versions, including Tables 3–5, H.1 and K.1 and Figures 1, I.1 and L.1. No scores, rankings or qualitative findings change.

T1.justification: The data-tuple definitions, length-conditioned Diversity Decile mapping and change-in-decile definition remain identical in Sections 4.1 and 5.2.2. No mathematical assumptions, derivations or proofs are added or revised.

C1.justification: The abstract, contribution list and Discussion retain the same claims about length bias, efficient diversity improvement, lightweight filtering, small-to-large transfer, length-adjusted evaluation and the released dataset.

C2.justification: The diversity–quality tradeoff interpretation, explanation for longer outputs, and limitations concerning single-metric filtering, story-only training and one tuning round remain identical in the Discussion, Limitations and Appendix G.

D1.justification: Implementation details, hyperparameters and resource destinations are unchanged. Page 1 displays full code and dataset URLs instead of descriptive labels, but inspection of the PDFs' embedded hyperlinks confirms identical GitHub and Hugging Face destinations.

R1.justification: Related work, citations and bibliography are identical. The relationship to DivPO and positioning around length-aware diversity alignment are unchanged.

P1.justification: The first-page resource footnote replaces its introductory phrase and descriptive link labels with Code/Dataset labels and full URLs. The arXiv version/date stamp also updates; all other wording and document structure remain identical.

P2.justification: The first-page footnote is locally reformatted, with full URLs wrapping across lines, and the margin stamp updates. All figures, tables, captions and remaining page layouts are identical.

improvement.justification: v4 makes existing resource addresses visible while retaining exactly the same hyperlink destinations. This offers a small presentation convenience; the scientific text, evidence, reproducibility details and appendices are unchanged, establishing no meaningful difference in overall paper quality.
